extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys, and patent office personnel (U.S.)
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory requirements and procedural standards for obtaining, prosecuting, and maintaining U.S. patents (as consolidated in the 1870 Act and related 1861–1866 provisions), covering patentability, specification/drawing/model requirements, fees, deadlines, marking, assignments, and office procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent term selection and fees (1861)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentees of designs may apply for a patent for the term of three and one-half years, seven years, or fourteen years, as the applicant may elect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee schedule: three years and six months — ten dollars; seven years — fifteen dollars; fourteen years — thirty dollars. Patentees of designs are entitled to a seven-year extension upon the same terms and restrictions as existing extension provisions (as provided at the time). (Note: later repealed as indicated in the text.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion/prosecution deadline for applications (two-year rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications for patents shall be completed and prepared for examination within two years after the filing of the petition, and in default thereof they shall be regarded as abandoned; and failure to prosecute within two years after any action (of which notice shall have been given) likewise results in abandonment unless delay was unavoidable and shown to the satisfaction of the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This abandonment rule applies to current and pending applications; exceptions require satisfactory proof of unavoidable delay to the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and timing for extension hearings and filings
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications for the extension of patents shall be filed at least ninety days before the expiration thereof; notice of the day set for the hearing shall be published for at least sixty days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet filing/timing and notice requirements may prevent consideration of extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent marking requirement and effect on damages
rubrics_metrics.description: Any article made or vended under the protection of letters-patent must be marked with the word 'patented' together with the day and year the patent was granted, or if impracticable because of the article's character, the notice with date must be affixed to the package or attached label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patentee (or those making/vending for them) fail to mark as required, in any suit for infringement no damages shall be recovered by the plaintiff except upon proof that the defendant was duly notified of the infringement and continued thereafter to make or vend the patented article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing and distribution of patent descriptions, claims, and drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner is authorized to print (or cause to be printed) ten copies of the description and claims and ten copies of the drawings of all patents granted; one copy shall be printed on parchment to be affixed to the letters-patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost limits are specified (text printing not to exceed two cents per hundred words per copy, drawings not to exceed fifty cents per copy); the work is under the Commissioner's direction and paid from the patent fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed copies of letters-patent as legal evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed copies of the letters-patent of the United States, with the seal of the Patent Office affixed and certified and signed by the Commissioner, shall be legal evidence of the contents of said letters-patent in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified printed copies are admissible as proof of patent contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term — seventeen years and prohibition on extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: All patents hereafter granted shall remain in force for the term of seventeen years from the date of issue; and all extension of such patents is hereby prohibited (in the 1861 act language; the consolidated 1870 act also sets seventeen-year term).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents cannot be extended beyond the statutory term under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners-in-chief qualifications and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiners-in-chief shall be persons of competent legal knowledge and scientific ability, whose duty is, on written petition of the appellant, to revise and determine upon the validity of adverse decisions of examiners on applications, reissues, and interference cases; and to hear/report on claims for extensions when required by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualification requirement emphasizes both legal and scientific competence; examiners-in-chief perform appellate and interference adjudicative functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification: written description and enablement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Before receiving a patent, the inventor shall file in the Patent Office a written description of the invention and of the manner and process of making, constructing, compounding, and using it, 'in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable any person skilled in the art or science to which it appertains ... to make, construct, compound, and use the same.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For machines, the inventor must explain the principle thereof and the best mode contemplated of applying that principle so as to distinguish it from other inventions; the specification must particularly point out and distinctly claim the part, improvement, or combination which is claimed as the invention; the specification and claim must be signed by the inventor and attested by two witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings requirement and formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: When the nature of the case admits of drawings, the applicant shall furnish one copy signed by the inventor or his attorney-in-fact and attested by two witnesses, which shall be filed in the Patent Office; a copy furnished by the Patent Office shall be attached to the patent as part of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings become part of the patent; formal attestation and filing are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens for compositions of matter
rubrics_metrics.description: When the invention is of a composition of matter, the applicant, if required by the Commissioner, shall furnish specimens of ingredients and of the composition sufficient in quantity for the purpose of experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner may demand specimens to allow testing of the composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models where admissible
rubrics_metrics.description: In all cases which admit of representation by model, the applicant, if required by the Commissioner, shall furnish one of convenient size to exhibit advantageously the several parts of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner can require a physical model to illustrate the invention's parts and operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath of inventor: original and first inventor; citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall make oath or affirmation that he verily believes himself to be the original and first inventor or discoverer of the invention, that he does not know nor believe the same was ever before known or used, and shall state his country of citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oath or affirmation may be made before authorized persons in the U.S. or, for applicants abroad, before certain U.S. diplomatic/consular officers or foreign notaries as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner examination and utility/importance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing of the application and payment of duty, the Commissioner shall cause an examination to be made of the alleged new invention; if it appears that the claimant is justly entitled to a patent under the law, and that the same is sufficiently useful and important, the Commissioner shall issue a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an express standard of usefulness and importance in the Commissioner's exercise of granting patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / prior publication / public use / statutory bar (two-year rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who has invented or discovered a new and useful art, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter, or any useful improvement, 'not known or used by others in this country, and not patented, or described in any printed publication in this or any foreign country, before his invention ... and not in public use or on sale for more than two years prior to his application' may obtain a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This states the requirements of novelty (not previously known/used/patented/described) and imposes a two-year statutory bar for public use or sale prior to application (unless abandonment is shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign patent/filing effect and co-term expiry
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall be debarred from receiving a patent by reason of having first patented in a foreign country, provided the invention was not introduced into public use in the United States for more than two years prior to the U.S. application; the U.S. patent shall expire at the same time as the foreign patent (or the one having the shortest term), but in no case shall it be in force more than seventeen years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign patenting is allowed but creates co-term or shorter-term limitations and is subject to the two-year U.S. public-use bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final fee payment timeline and consequences (six-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall be dated as of a day not later than six months after it was passed and allowed, and notice thereof sent to the applicant; if the final fee is not paid within said six months, the patent shall be withheld and the invention described shall become public property as against the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-payment of the final fee within six months results in the patent being withheld and loss of exclusivity as to the applicant; special provisions apply to patents allowed prior to certain enactments as noted in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to reapply after failure to pay final fee
rubrics_metrics.description: A person for whom a patent was ordered to issue upon payment of the final fee but who failed to pay within six months shall have the right to make an application for a patent the same as an original application, provided such application be made within two years after the allowance of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This right to refile limits liability for manufacture/use prior to issue and sets a two-year window for a renewed application; applies to cases where patents were allowed but final fee unpaid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting/reissuing to assignees and inventor's oath requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents may be granted or reissued to the assignee of the inventor, the assignment first entered of record in the Patent Office; but the application for the patent shall be made and the specifications sworn to by the inventor (and in case of reissue if he be living).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment of record is required for assignee patents, but inventor's own sworn application/specification remains a formal prerequisite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death of inventor — executor/administrator rights
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person having made a new invention dies before a patent is granted, the right to apply for and obtain the patent devolves on his executor or administrator in trust for heirs (or, if testate, in trust for devisees) on the same terms and conditions as if claimed by the deceased in his lifetime; the required oath/affirmation shall be varied so it can be made by such legal representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides succession rules allowing legal representatives to pursue patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment recording to be effective against subsequent purchasers
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent or interest therein shall be assignable by an instrument in writing; such assignment, grant, or conveyance shall be void as against any subsequent purchaser or mortgagee for a valuable consideration without notice unless recorded in the Patent Office within three months from the date thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To protect priority vs. subsequent purchasers, recording within three months is required; otherwise assignment may be void against later bona fide purchasers without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior user right for specific articles made/sold before application
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who purchased of the inventor, or with his knowledge and consent constructed any newly invented machine or article prior to the inventor's application, or sold or used one so constructed, shall have the right to use and vend the specific thing so made or purchased without liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves a limited prior user right for specific items made or sold with inventor's knowledge before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for false marking or counterfeit patent marks
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person marks upon any thing made, used, or sold by him the name or imitation of the name of a patentee (or affixes 'patent', 'patentee', 'letters-patent', or like words) for the purpose of deceiving the public, without consent of the patentee, he shall be liable to a penalty of not less than one hundred dollars with costs; one moiety to the person who sues and the other moiety to the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory civil penalty enforceable in district court of the U.S.; false marking is actionable and financially penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat filing for additional maturation time
rubrics_metrics.description: A citizen who has made a new invention and desires further time to mature it may, on payment of the required duty, file in the Patent Office a caveat setting forth the design and distinguishing characteristics and praying protection of his right until he has matured the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveat provides provisional protection while inventor develops the invention; must be filed and duty paid as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal fee from primary examiner to examiners-in-chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon appealing for the first time from the decision of the primary examiner to the examiners-in-chief, the appellant shall pay a fee of ten dollars into the Patent Office; no such appeal shall be allowed until the fee is paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural fee requirement for initiating appellate review within the office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent contents: short title and annexed specification/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall contain a short title or description correctly indicating the nature and design of the invention, a grant to the patentee for the term of seventeen years of the exclusive right to make, use, and vend the invention throughout the United States and Territories referring to the specification for particulars; a copy of the specifications and drawings shall be annexed to the patent and be a part thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal content and attachment requirements ensure the patent document clearly identifies the invention and includes the specification/drawings as integral parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner authority to require legible/printed papers at applicant cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may require all papers filed in the Patent Office, if not correctly, legibly and clearly written, to be printed at the cost of the party filing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures legibility and uniformity of papers; cost borne by filer if Commissioner so directs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner rulemaking and printing powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner, subject to approval of the Secretary of the Interior, may from time to time establish rules and regulations (not inconsistent with law) for conduct of proceedings in the Patent Office; he may also print copies of specifications, drawings, claims of current issues, and copies of laws, decisions, rules and circulars necessary for public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative delegation allows the Commissioner to manage procedures and public dissemination of patent materials.
